summary: Fredun Pharmaceuticals makes medicines in a factory near Mumbai and sells most of them abroad, and is now adding pet-health, supplement and wellness brands.
description: A medicine such as a blood-pressure tablet must be made, packed, approved in each country that buys it, and sold to someone who will pay. Fredun does this for generic medicines (copies of medicines whose original patents have ended) in its own factory in Palghar, near Mumbai. Distributors and importers in many countries buy them, mostly in Africa, Southeast Asia, the former Soviet region and Latin America. Government agencies also buy medicines through public tenders. Over the past few years Fredun has added pet medicines, food supplements, skin-care products, support braces and a wellness range, which it presents as a wider healthcare business.
money: Fredun earns money when a distributor, importer, government agency or other customer pays for the medicines and products it ships. Its main costs are the chemical ingredients, factory work, getting each product approved in each country, selling and advertising, and interest on loans. Newer consumer brands usually cost money to launch before they bring in much, so adding many at once can hold back profit.
customers: Overseas distributors and importers are the main buyers of its medicines. State government agencies buy through tenders, which are formal bids to supply a fixed quantity. Other drug companies sometimes pay Fredun to make products that they sell under their own names. Pet owners, vets, shops and online sellers buy the consumer and pet products.
drivers: How many countries approve and buy its medicines, the price of ingredients, what it earns on each product, how quickly overseas customers pay, and whether the new brands bring in sales that cover their launch costs.

groups.title: Branded generic medicines for export
groups.examples: Medicines sold under its own Fredun Gx brand, such as treatments for high blood pressure and diabetes, and antiretroviral medicines used to treat HIV.
groups.explanation: A generic medicine has the same active ingredient as an older, original medicine. Fredun sells many under its own brand name. To sell in a country, each product needs a registration, the local drug regulator’s approval. Its annual report says it holds more than 800 registrations and has more being prepared. It describes this as the company’s largest and longest-established business.

groups.title: Medicines made for others and sold through tenders
groups.examples: Products made for other companies to sell under their own names, and medicines supplied to government agencies.
groups.explanation: When Fredun makes a product for another company, that company sells it under its own name, which is called OEM (original equipment manufacturer) work. In a tender, an agency such as a state medical-supplies body invites suppliers to bid. The winner supplies a fixed quantity at the agreed price, which can mean steady orders but little room to raise prices.

groups.title: Pet health and veterinary products
groups.examples: Animal medicines, pet diagnostics, pet food and pet shops under the Freossi, One Pet Stop and Wagr names.
groups.explanation: Freossi is Fredun’s pet-health brand. One Pet Stop is a pet retail business that it bought, and Wagr is a pet retail business, selling in shops and online, in which it has invested. Fredun wants these together to cover what a pet owner buys, from medicines and tests to food. They are newer than its medicine exports, so there is less history to show how profitable they will be.

groups.title: Supplements, skin care and home-health products
groups.examples: Supplement brands such as Mamalait and Fredmax, the BeautyFred skin-care range, and braces, nebulisers and home monitors.
groups.explanation: Nutraceuticals are food supplements sold for health purposes. Cosmeceuticals are skin products that contain added active ingredients. A nebuliser turns liquid medicine into a mist that can be breathed in. These are sold to consumers and through shops, so they depend on advertising and shelf space as well as on the product.

groups.title: Premium wellness and hormone-health range
groups.examples: The DAULCÉL wellness brand and a range of hormone-health products, both launched in FY 2025–26.
groups.explanation: These are the newest lines. Fredun describes them with terms such as longevity and cellular vitality, which are the company’s own marketing language. This notebook does not assess any health claim made for a product, and there is not yet history showing how these lines will sell.

basics.title: What is a generic medicine?
basics.text: A generic medicine has the same active ingredient as an original medicine that was developed and patented by another company. Once the patent ends, other makers can sell it, usually at a lower price. Many companies make the same generics, so price competition is a constant feature of the business.

basics.title: Why does a medicine need registration in every country?
basics.text: Each country’s drug regulator decides which medicines may be sold. A company must submit documents and often samples before it can sell a product there. The approvals take time and money, but a registered product can be hard for a rival to copy quickly. Fredun’s report says it owns or co-owns many of its registrations.

basics.title: What is a bonus issue?
basics.text: In a bonus issue a company gives existing shareholders extra shares for free in proportion to what they hold. Fredun gave shareholders two new shares for every one held in July 2026, so the number of shares tripled. Nothing is paid in and the company is not worth more because of it. Per-share figures are therefore restated, so check the share count before comparing them across years.

steps.title: Get the product approved for a country
steps.text: Fredun prepares the registration documents and waits for the country’s regulator to approve each medicine.

steps.title: Make the medicine in the factory
steps.text: Buy active ingredients and other materials, make tablets, capsules or other forms, test them and pack them. Its annual report says it runs one integrated factory and plans a new facility, which it expected to start operating in October 2026.

steps.title: Ship to the buyer
steps.text: The buyer may be a distributor in another country, a government agency that won a tender, or another drug company that sells the product under its own name.

steps.title: Invoice and wait for payment
steps.text: Overseas customers may pay in a foreign currency and take some time. Revenue is recorded when the sale is made, but cash arrives later, and some customers may pay late or not in full.

steps.title: Spend on the next set of products
steps.text: Fredun spends on new registrations, new brands and extra factory space before they earn. This is why growth and profit can move differently.

specifics.title: The medicine business pays for the experiments
specifics.text: Fredun’s report calls the medicine business the main cash-generating engine that supports its newer ventures. If medicine prices or export orders weaken, the money available for pet, supplement and wellness launches also shrinks.

specifics.title: Many new businesses at once
specifics.text: In one year the company bought a pet retail network, opened a pet diagnostic centre, new brands and a new factory plot. Each needs people, stock and marketing. Read whether each new business reports its own sales, because the company’s own description does not show how much each one earns.

specifics.title: The company’s description is promotional
specifics.text: Management’s section of the annual report uses words such as landmark year, record and stellar. These are the company’s views, not independent findings. Look for the figures and dates they rest on.

specifics.title: Bonus shares change the share count, not the business
specifics.text: After the July 2026 bonus issue the number of shares tripled. Profit per share would fall by the same factor if profit stayed the same, so per-share numbers from before and after must be put on the same basis before comparing.

watch: How much of sales still comes from medicines sold abroad?
The export medicine business is the established part; the new businesses are not yet proven.

Look in the annual report and results notes for the split between exports, government supply, contract manufacturing and the new consumer brands. Check whether the share of the new brands is rising and whether they are reported separately.
Does profit keep pace as sales grow?
Sales can rise quickly without profit rising by as much.

Compare the growth in sales with the growth in operating profit and the profit margin, which is profit as a share of sales. In its 6 August 2026 results, sales and profit rose by similar proportions, so the margin hardly moved.
How long does Fredun wait to be paid?
Overseas distributors and government agencies pay on different schedules and some in foreign currencies.

Check receivables, which are bills issued but not yet paid, as a share of sales, and compare them across years. Read what the company says about foreign-currency risk and about customers in particular countries.
Will the new factory space be used?
A new facility adds costs such as depreciation and staff even if orders do not arrive.
Look for the date the new facility actually starts operating, what it will make, and whether capital spending was funded by borrowing. Compare planned capacity with orders already in hand.
Are the new brands earning their launch costs?
Pet, supplement, skin-care and wellness brands need advertising and stock before sales build.

Look for separate sales or profit for each new line, any acquisition costs, and the stock held in shops. Treat claims about the size of future markets as the company’s view and check what sales it has actually reported.
risks: Regulators or buyers change the rules
A country can delay or refuse a registration, change its import rules or change what it will pay. Fredun sells in many such markets.
A failed quality check or a recall can stop sales and damage the relationship with distributors.
The cost of active ingredients and the exchange rate can change faster than Fredun can change its selling prices.
Distributors and agencies in other countries can delay payment or fail to pay, which ties up cash.
Too many new businesses at once
Launching pet, supplement, skin-care, device and wellness lines together stretches management and money, and some may not earn back their costs.
A small company with a short record on its new lines
The new lines are recent and their results are described mainly by the company itself.
context: November 2026: more pet businesses and a plan to list on a second exchange

Fredun’s 6 November 2026 results release says total income for April–September 2026 was almost double that of a year earlier, and profit grew a little faster than sales. In September 2026 it bought Furlicks, a pet-supplement brand, and a 26 per cent stake in Goodman Vetcare, a pet-care business. On 5 November 2026 its board approved applying to list its shares on the National Stock Exchange as well as the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), where it trades now; that is a plan, not yet approved by the exchange. The quarterly figures are unaudited, meaning only reviewed, not fully checked, by the auditors. The full-year figures at the end of this page cover an earlier period.

financialNotes.title: Read the medicine business and the new lines separately
financialNotes.text: Check how much of sales comes from exports and government supply compared with the new consumer lines, and compare profit growth with sales growth. A per-share figure must be put on the same share count after the July 2026 bonus issue. Verified full-year figures for this profile have not yet been added, so the financial table below is marked as awaiting verification.

stepsTitle: From an approval to an overseas payment.

quick.title: What it does
quick.text: Fredun makes copies of established medicines (generics) in a factory near Mumbai and sells most of them abroad. It is also adding pet-health, supplement and wellness brands.

quick.title: Who pays
quick.text: Overseas distributors and importers buy most of its medicines. State agencies buy through tenders, which are formal bids to supply. Other drug firms pay it to make their products. Pet owners, vets and shops buy pet products.

quick.title: How it earns
quick.text: It earns by selling the medicines and products it ships, and by making products for other companies to sell under their own names.

quick.title: What it spends on
quick.text: Chemical ingredients, factory work, getting each product approved in each country, selling and advertising, and interest on loans. New brands cost money to launch before they earn much.

helps.title: The medicine business earns the cash
helps.text: Fredun’s FY 2025–26 annual report calls its generic-medicine business the main cash-generating engine. That cash pays for its newer pet and wellness ventures.

helps.title: Sales across many countries
helps.text: Fredun exports mainly to Africa, Southeast Asia, the former Soviet region and Latin America. Its annual report says it holds more than 800 product approvals, and each approval is another country where it can sell that product.

helps.title: Several kinds of customer
helps.text: Distributors, importers, government agencies, other drug companies, vets and pet owners all buy from it, so it does not depend on one kind of buyer.

hurts.title: Countries can change the rules
hurts.text: Fredun’s annual report names regulatory compliance as a main risk. A country can delay or refuse a product approval or change its import rules, which stops sales there.

hurts.title: Quality and supply problems
hurts.text: The report also names product quality and supply-chain continuity. A failed quality check or a missing ingredient can hold up shipments.

hurts.title: Many new businesses at once
hurts.text: In FY 2025–26 it bought a pet retail business, opened a pet diagnostic centre, launched new brands and bought a plot for a new factory, and in September 2026 it bought more pet businesses. Its report lists running new businesses as a main risk; each needs money and management time.

hurts.title: Currency swings
hurts.text: Most sales are abroad, and the report names foreign exchange as a main risk. A change in exchange rates can change what Fredun receives in rupees.
